text:
A fourth-round pick who needed 61 AHL games to get here, Adam Wilsby is now logging 20:18 a night on Nashville's blue line, and it's climbed past 21 minutes over his last ten games. That's a real role for a defenseman with 81 NHL games before this season.

The points (8 in 22, none on the power play) won't make anyone look twice, and our wins-added ranking, which only counts goals, has him near the bottom of the league. The five-on-five numbers tell a better story. The Predators take 53.5% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on the ice, about 10 points better than without him.

He gets there with his feet. NHL EDGE has him in the 97th percentile for top speed and for bursts over 20 mph, and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him carrying the puck in on 53% of his entries last season and reaching the home-plate area more than 94% of defensemen. Evolving-Hockey had him just above replacement last season. Watch whether the bigger minutes hold up against top lines.
